title.narrative: Danish Human Rights Institute: Human Rights-Based Approach to Public Emergencies: Promoting Sustainable Recovery From COVID19 and Building Resilience

description.narrative: The objective of the project is to contribute to a sustainable pandemic recovery that realises human rights and the SDGs with a focus on those furthest left behind, while increasing resilience to human rights violations in future crises. The objective will be achieved through interventions at the national level in two developing countries (Honduras and Indonesia), complemented by regional and global interventions. DIHR will focus on gender and intersectionality, including indigenous women and girls, in all activities.

title.narrative: Output 2.1. Regional and global dialogue. Four side events (in conjunction with the HRC intersessional and the HLPF in 2022, 2023) are organized, well-attended by a diverse range of stakeholders and used as a platform by states to report and share good practices.
Number of events held and well attended.

actual.value: 2 events organised in the context of the Human Rights Council intersessional meeting on the 2030 Agenda and human rights and the High-Level Political Forum on Sustainable Development in New York in July 2023. State representatives from 4 countries Luxemburg, Finland, Colombia and the Philippines participated alongside civil society representatives of human rights actors. The events were well attended and focused on different aspects of the human rights-based approach to sustainable recovery and preparation for future crises.

2 side events organised and held as planned. The January 2022 Human Rights Council intersessional meeting on human rights and the 2030 Agenda side event and the side event at the HLPF 2022 brought together multiple stakeholders including State actors (Ambassadors from Guatemala and Luxemburg, Ukraine, Chile and Marshall Islands), major groups/civil society/rights-holder organisations, representatives of the corporate sector and the UN system. The events served as opportunities for stock-taking and sharing of good practices and lessons learned from the recovery efforts and a discussion of resilience to future crises. The events reached a diverse online audience of around 250 participants.

title.narrative: Policy Briefs tailored to generate dialogue published & dialogues conducted with civil society, government and policymakers.

target.value: 1. One to two policy briefs or other form of documentation produced; 2. Policy dialogues initiated in cooperation with civil society and rights-holder groups (including women representatives of these groups).

actual.value: An advocacy report drafted on the right to work and decent work in the context of sustainable recovery and building resilience towards future crises in Indonesia based on observations and recommendations from both international human rights mechanisms and from the NHRI of Indonesia, Komnas HAM. The report advocates for the Government to address these key human rights issues as part of the Government’s plans for following up to Indonesia’s 4th UPR and for the Government to link the right to work and decent work with the national implementation of SDG targets. The report is expected to be finalised in Q1 of 2023. The national dialogue was postponed to Q1 of 2023, but a meeting was held with the Ministry of National Development Planning (Bappenas) on SDGs implementation, data and monitoring initiatives and to introduce the upcoming report on the right to work and decent work in 2022.

target.value: 1. – 2. Policy dialogues continue, and at least one policy recommendation is being acted upon by State actors to improve vulnerable and marginalised groups’ access to sustainable development.

actual.value: Komnas HAM published a report describing the implications of the Covid-19 pandemic on the right to work, decent work and social security of migrant workers, domestic workers, and precarious workers. The report also provides guidance for the Government of Indonesia on how to take actions on sustainable recovery and build resilience to future crises based on human rights and SDG targets. Two policy dialogues were held on 8 May 2023 based on the report. One dialogue targeted the government and relevant ministries, the other dialogue targeted civil society organisations representing rights-holders. The report was welcomed by all stakeholders at the policy dialogues. The target for 2023 has largely been met, as a representative from the Ministry of Labour gave the news that the Government has included recommendations from Komnas HAM regarding the rights of domestic workers in the upcoming Bill of Protection for Domestic Workers.

title.narrative: Output 2.2. African NHRIs are actively engaged in experience-sharing and advocacy on human rights-based approaches to sustainable recovery and disaster preparedness.
Number of experience-sharing and capacity-building workshops organised and well-attended and number of positive examples of NHRIs having engaged with regional human rights mechanisms.

target.value: 1. 1 regional advocacy event 2. At least one example of African NHRIs having engaged with African regional human rights mechanisms

actual.value: 2 Regional Advocacy events took place and 4 African NHRIs engaged with the African Commission on Human and People’s Rights.

target.value: 1. 1 Regional experience-sharing workshop 2. 1 Virtual capacity building workshop

actual.value: Experience sharing and capacity building for African NHRIs took place in the form of two online workshops with the participation of DIHR, NANHRI, external experts and representatives of NHRIs in Kenya, Uganda, Malawi and the Gambia. NHRIs in Uganda, Malawi and the Gambia were supported with mini grants and technical support to undertake research and gather data on gaps in social protection for particular groups and document lessons from the pandemic. These case studies will feed into a report to be published in 2023 – related to output 3 and be used as basis for advocacy nationally and regionally.

title.narrative: Improved technical capacities and knowledge on indigenous people´ rights and relation to the SDGs are demonstrated by CONADEH and rights-holder organisations.

target.value: Significant capacity and knowledge demonstrated (through data analysis and engagement in recovery planning and policy).

actual.value: CEHPRODEC, a local CSO in Honduras, monitored indigenous peoples´ rights using the Indigenous Navigator and elaborated a report describing the developments and gaps regarding three indigenous peoples in Honduras (Pech, Lenca and Tolupanes) in 6 communities. The data collection improved awareness and capacities of the indigenous peoples of their human rights. An advocacy dialogue was held in November 2023, in which findings and requests were presented to State representatives (amongst others CONADEH, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Health, and the Ministry of Human Rights). This helped direct attention of duty bearers, and the information fills a gap in official information about indigenous peoples in Honduras. Some public authorities expressed commitment to address the issues identified and to expand the analysis to other indigenous peoples in Honduras. CONADEH, the NHRI, joined the process and information will feed into the Human Rights Observatory recently set up by CONADEH.

target.value: Some capacity built and demonstrated (through data collection)

actual.value: The capacity building activities have commenced. Indigenous peoples’ leaders engage with the project and use the Indigenous Navigator to monitor the realisation of indigenous peoples’ rights in Honduras. DIHR also engaged in the multistakeholder roundtable on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights focusing on the National Action Plan (NAP) on Business and Human Rights and focused on the need to ensure participation of disproportionately impacted groups, notably the indigenous peoples in Honduras.

title.narrative: Output 3.1. Guidance and good practices on the Pledge commitments are compiled and presented in a user-friendly way.
Number of publications with guidance and good practices that are published and shared at global and national events.

target.value: 1 publication: Good practices, ideally one per pledge commitment

actual.value: 2 publications published: one on good practices on implementing the sustainable recovery pledge and one on social protection focusing on marginalised groups in Africa.

target.value: 1 publication: An annotated version of the pledge pointing to key guidance on how to implement and monitor pledge commitments

actual.value: The report “Sustainable Recovery Pledge: Good Practices for Change” was drafted (only published at the beginning of January 2023). The report is a collection of good practices showcasing some of the recovery efforts following up on the launch of the Sustainable Recovery Pledge. The drafting of the Africa regional publication on advancing the right to social protection began in 2022 and will be published in 2023 incorporating case studies from Malawi, Uganda, the Gambia and Kenya.

title.narrative: State actors, NHRIs, civil society and rights-holder organisations are engaged in dialogue and peer-learning on human rights-based approaches to sustainable recovery and emergency preparedness informed by evidence.

Number of state actors that have shared experiences on how they are implementing their Pledge commitments and preparing for future crises in international fora; Number of NHRIs in the Africa region and in Honduras and Indonesia that have engaged with state actors, regional and international human rights mechanisms to influence the recovery based on evidence; Number of rights-holder organisations (and among these women representatives) that are empowered to collect disaggregated data and engage in recovery policy dialogue in Honduras and Indonesia.

target.value: State actors from at least 5 countries, including developing countries, 5 NHRIs (including Komnas HAM in Indonesia and CONADEH in Honduras), at least 4 rights-holder organisations.

actual.value: State representatives from 8 countries (the Ukraine, Chile, Marshall Islands, Guatemala, Luxemburg, Finland, Colombia and the Philippines) discussed how human rights should be at the center of preparedness for future crises and shocks based on lessons learnt from the Covid-19 pandemic in events organised under the project. 4 African NHRIs (The Gambia, Malawi, Uganda and Kenya) engaged with international and regional human rights bodies in addition to the engagement of the NHRI in Indonesia and Honduras with state actors (6 NHRIs total). 20 CSOs in Indonesia and one in Honduras plus indigenous leaders in Honduras continued to engage in evidence collection and started engaging with state actors on issues identified.
